The U.S. Department of Education provides more than $120 billion in financial aid to help pay for college or career school each year. Make sure you develop a plan early and start by filling out your FAFSA form . In addition to grants and scholarships, you may qualify for loans with a lower interest rate than some private loans. Types of federal financial aid Grants According to the FSA, a grant is a form of financial aid that typically doesn’t have to be repaid (unless, for example, you withdraw from school and owe a refund, or you receive a TEACH Grant and don’t complete your service obligation). A variety of federal grants are available, including Pell Grants, Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grants (FSEOG), Teacher Education Assistance for College and Higher Education (TEACH) Grants, and Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grants. Scholarships Scholarships, which are often based on academic merit, talent, or a particular area of study, can make a real difference in helping you manage your education expenses. Loans When you receive a student loan , you are borrowing money to attend a college or career school. You must repay the loan as well as the interest that accrues. It is important to understand your repayment options so you can successfully repay your loan. Recently interest rates for federal loans were announced. U.S. Gridded Methane Emissions The gridded EPA U.S. methane greenhouse gas inventory (gridded methane GHGI) includes time series of annual methane emission maps with 0.1° x 0.1° (~ 10 x 10 km) spatial and monthly temporal resolution for the contiguous United States (CONUS). This gridded methane inventory is designed to be consistent with methane emissions from the U.S. EPA Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks (U.S. GHGI). The gridded methane GHGI dataset includes annual methane emission fluxes for over 25 inventory emission source categories, including those from agriculture, petroleum and natural gas systems, coal mining, and waste. Gridded methane emissions data are generated by allocating national annual U.S. GHGI methane emissions from individual source categories to a 0.1° x 0.1° CONUS grid, using a series of spatial and temporal 'proxy' datasets at the state, county, and grid levels. Where possible, proxy data are the same data used to develop the U.S. GHGI so that the gridded emissions can be, as closely as possible, a spatial and temporal representation of the national-level U.S. GHGI. Between July and September, the economy expanded by 0.7%, accelerating from the previous three months, official figures show. The robust growth suggests a far more resilient economy than expected over the summer, despite the impact of higher energy prices from the Iran war. Strong growth in the services sector - the largest part of the economy, which includes non-physical goods such as consultancy services and computer programming as well as hotels and restaurants - helped boost the numbers. Within services, computer programming registered its fastest growth for the past three years, helped by cloud computing and AI-linked spending. The boost from computer programming and consultancy services has been the biggest driver of growth so far this year. pages.text: UK Reader Awards 2026: Winners Revealed | National Geographic By Editors of National Geographic Traveller (UK) Published September 30, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). It’s been an interesting year in travel — more reason than ever for us to reinstate our Reader Awards. We wanted to know what inspires you when booking a trip and where’s really captured your imagination in the past year. What came across most keenly was your continuing desire to explore, seek out new experiences and connect with both the environment and other cultures. The winners’ list indicates a return to familiar destinations on the UK’s doorstep, perhaps a reflection of the challenges — tight finances, fractious politics, Middle East strife — that have affected travel in 2026. But more far-flung destinations are also among the 16 category finalists, testament to your unshakeable enthusiasm for adventure. People’s Choice: Italy Food and beauty are the secular religions that elevate Italy to another level. No brochure flags up either directly. Why would they? Both are factored into the equation wherever you go, whether to Naples for pizza, Florence for art or Sardinia for improbably perfect beaches. Runner-up Japan equally justifies its popularity. Now almost a bargain due to persistent low inflation and a weak yen, the country remains distinct in an increasingly homogenised world. pages.text: Ukraine appeal IOC decision to reinstate Russia - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 By Elizabeth Botcherby BBC Sport journalist Published 29 July 2026 Ukraine's National Olympic Committee has launched an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport against the International Olympic Committee's decision to provisionally reinstate Russia to its competitions. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) suspended the Russian Olympic Committee (ROC) in 2023 in response to the war in Ukraine but lifted the ban on 7 July 2026, stating it was "no longer applicable" , external . That decision opens the door for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games and is the latest step in the country's reinstatement to international competition, with the IOC previously recommending in December 2025 that federations readmit Russian and Belarusian Under-23 athletes. However, the National Olympic Committee (NOC) of Ukraine said the IOC's decision is "premature" and "violates" the Olympic Charter. "The position of the NOC of Ukraine is based on the fact that the IOC's decision was made prematurely and without proper verification of whether the violations - which led to the suspension of the ROC following the appeal by the NOC of Ukraine on October 6, 2023 - had actually been resolved," an NOC statement said. The Census Bureau and other state and federal agencies are responsible for assigning geographic identifiers, or GEOIDs, to geographic entities to facilitate the organization, presentation, and exchange of geographic and statistical data. GEOIDs are numeric codes that uniquely identify all administrative/legal and statistical geographic areas for which the Census Bureau tabulates data. From Alaska, the largest state, to the smallest census block in New York City, every geographic area has a unique GEOID. Some of the most common administrative/legal and statistical geographic entities with unique GEOIDs include states, counties, congressional districts, core based statistical areas (metropolitan and micropolitan areas), census tracts, block groups and census blocks. Data users rely on GEOIDs to join the appropriate demographic data from censuses and surveys, such as the American Community Survey (ACS), to various levels of geography for data analysis, interpretation and mapping. pages.text: Unemployment scams | USAGov Skip to main content Unemployment scams Scammers can file unemployment benefits using other people's names and personal information. Learn how to protect yourself and your benefits from this type of identity theft. Warning signs of unemployment scams You can experience an unemployment scam whether you apply for unemployment benefits or not. Understand what you could receive or undergo as a warning sign of an unemployment scam: If you applied for unemployment benefits: The application you filled out online may have been on a fraudulent website, not from your state unemployment office. You were approved for unemployment insurance payments but have not received them. The unemployment office rejected your application for benefits because they already received a claim under your name. If you did not apply for unemployment benefits: A notice from your state unemployment office. A notice from your former employer about an unemployment benefits application that you did not apply for. Form 1099-G that shows you got unemployment benefit payments you were not expecting and never received. The 1099-G you receive may be sent from a state where you have never been employed. A direct deposit from your state unemployment office that you did not expect to receive. A call from someone claiming to be from your state unemployment. office saying money was deposited into your account by mistake. pages.text: Union Resources | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Union Resources The Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) administers provisions of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA), which promotes labor-management transparency by making available reports showing unions’ financial condition and employer expenditures for their activities in persuading workers during union organizing campaigns. It also promotes labor union democracy and financial integrity through adopting and enforcing standards for union officer elections and union trusteeships and safeguards for union assets. OLMS also administers the standards of conduct provisions of the Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 ( CSRA ) and the Foreign Service Act of 1980, which extend comparable protections to Federal labor unions. A union that represents only employees of state, county, or municipal governments is not subject to the LMRDA or the CSRA. See 29 CFR Part 451 and the OLMS Interpretative Manual Definitions section for further information concerning labor organization coverage under the LMRDA. OLMS has the authority to enforce certain provisions of the LMRDA. However, some provisions of the LMRDA such as the Bill of Rights and the fiduciary standards for union officers can only be enforced by union members through a private suit in Federal district court. See the OLMS Interpretative Manual Enforcement section . The CSRA standards of conduct regulations also incorporate many of the LMRDA provisions. A new report by UNESCO and University College London, presented at COP31, finds that AI models answer 90% of climate questions correctly but quickly abandon scientific facts when challenged by users—a warning to policymakers and researchers considering AI for climate policy development. Accuracy also varies widely across 13 different languages, reflecting differences in available training data, with better outcomes in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese and lower marks in languages such as Hindi, Urdu and Swahili. Eight times out of 10, models pivoted at the very first sign that the user mildly disagreed, confirming alarming errors such as ‘Co2 is not the main driver of climate change. pages.text: Universal Design | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Universal Design More in This Section Close Accessible Technology Communications Access Health Care Housing Personal Assistance Services Transportation Universal Design Universal design (UD) is a strategy for making products, environments, operational systems, and services welcoming and usable to the widest range of people possible. The key principles of UD are simplicity, flexibility, and efficiency. Whether we realize it or not, most of us benefit from UD on a daily basis. Originally developed in response to the needs of the aging population and people with disabilities, UD now increases access to products, places, and services for all populations. Companies that embrace UD in their facilities, programs, and services recognize that their workforce and customers have a broad range of abilities, ages, reading levels, learning styles, languages, etc.—and an even wider variety of needs and expectations. Good customer service means providing every customer with a welcoming environment, respectful treatment, and needed information. This goes for the workforce as well. UD provides an important tool set for companies seeking to provide such advantages for both their customers and their employees. UD is a lens through which every aspect of a business can be viewed, and a set of tools by which products, services, customer satisfaction, and employee attraction and retention can be improved. The incredible speed and precise control enabled by power electronics also create enhanced opportunities for how electricity is generated, delivered, and managed. Power electronics control and transform electricity to make it useful for modern digital technologies. For example, when you charge your phone or laptop, power electronics change the 120-volt alternating current (AC) power from the wall outlet into low-voltage direct current (DC) for its battery. It rapidly switches the current on and off so your device charges safely without getting too hot. Urinary Tract Infection Basics For Everyone Sept. 22, 2026 Español Key points Do you have pain or burning when you urinate? You might have a urinary tract infection (UTI). UTIs are common infections that happen when bacteria enter the urethra and infect the urinary tract. Antibiotics treat UTIs. A healthcare professional can determine if you have a UTI and what antibiotic you need. Overview The urinary tract includes the bladder, urethra and kidneys (see figure). Urinary tract infections or UTIs are common infections that happen when bacteria, often from the skin or rectum, enter the urethra and infect the urinary tract. Female urinary tract Bacteria from the skin or rectum can travel up the urethra and cause a bladder infection. Types A bladder infection (cystitis) is the most common type of UTI. A k idney infection (pyelonephritis) is less common than bladder infection but is more serious. A total of 47 men – they were all male – have been killed by states operating the death penalty in the course of the year. That was almost double the number in 2024, amounting to the greatest frenzy of capital punishment bloodletting in the US since 2009. The dramatic jump in the practice of state killing will further separate the US from almost all other developed countries . Only Japan, Singapore and Taiwan have staged executions in recent years. More than 2,500 flights into or out of the US were delayed and 325 flights cancelled on Monday morning, a significant drop from the thousands delayed and cancelled on Friday, according to the latest data from FlightAware. "What you saw on Friday was very, very old equipment that had a heart attack," President Donald Trump said on Monday. Asked by reporters if he took any responsibility for the ground stop, Trump said he did not. "I don't take any responsibility," Trump said, praising his officials. "They did a great job, Secretary Duffy, acted incredibly." "The only responsibility should be, for 40 years they should have done this, with this system that is probably on average 50 years old," he said. Trump called on Congress to "give us the money" to fix the US' air traffic control systems. Every US airline was affected by Friday's ground stop, which lasted for more than four hours. pages.text: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers 22 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Madeline Halpert BBC's Madeline Halpert explains why the US lost its measles elimination status and what it could mean. After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months. Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination". The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines. The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s. The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. pages.text: US National Security Agency's classified internal network reportedly goes offline Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters US National Security Agency's classified internal network reportedly goes offline 21 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ana Faguy Getty Images The NSA did not specify which internal services were affected but several media reports say it was the NSANet network A highly classified network used by the US National Security Agency (NSA) for internal communications went offline on Tuesday for an unspecified period of time, according to US media reports. The NSA - America's largest intelligence organisation - said it had experienced a "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance" but that "mission-critical capabilities" were not affected. The outage reportedly affected the NSANet network, which is how officials send and receive top secret or classified information. It comes after a string of technology outages in the US in recent days that have affected flights, banks and other infrastructure. "While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues," an NSA spokesperson said in a statement to the BBC. "NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events." The State Department's Rewards for Justice is also offering to potentially relocate the person who provides such details. President Donald Trump claimed last year that Iran's nuclear facilities had been "completely and totally obliterated " following a bombing campaign by the US and Israel. Iran insists its nuclear programme is peaceful and that it has no intention of developing a nuclear weapon. Meanwhile, the US military says it is setting up a task force to enhance Washington's efforts to restrict Iran's movement of weapons and sanctioned material across its borders. The US military's Central Command (Centcom) said Task Force Iron Gate would operate from Tampa, Florida, and would work with other US government agencies. As well as the movement of weapons, it will also focus on dual-use and illegal revenue streams. Centcom estimates that its naval blockade of Iran's ports has prevented the country from exporting more than $25bn in crude oil.
